raw_response:
Alright, let me sit down and think through this year's plan. I've been on this land 40 years, so I mostly know what I'm doing, but I still have to make choices every spring.

**My situation this year.** I'm 62. My wife passed some years back and my son's working in the city — sends money when he can but doesn't come back for planting. So it's me alone on the 10.1 mu. That's the biggest thing on my mind: I can't do what I did at 40. Chili is money, but picking chili three times a week in August with nobody helping? I'll regret it. So I keep chili modest.

**How I'll split the land.** Cotton is what I know best, and in our village that's what most of us do — the land on the west side suits it. I'll put about 6.5 mu in cotton. Then 2 mu in chili up near the road where I can irrigate easy and the ground is better. The remaining 1.6 mu I'll put in mungbean — light work, fixes the nitrogen, and I can eat some and sell the rest at the township market. Cotton after cotton year after year is no good, the mungbean patch rotates around.

**Cotton (6.5 mu).** I buy the Bt hybrid seed at the township store — 两系 type, about 80 yuan per mu of seed. I plant around April 20th if the soil's warm, maybe the 25th if it's still cold. I lay down compound fertilizer before planting, about 40 kg of 15-15-15 per mu as base, then topdress urea at squaring — maybe 10 kg per mu. That comes to roughly 13-14 kg N per mu total. The extension guy at the station said to do 15 kg but I find with our ground 13 is enough, my neighbor Old Wang tried 18 and didn't get more cotton out of it. 

Irrigation twice — once at squaring in June if it hasn't rained, once at boll-filling in late July. Water costs money from the well, electric pump, I pay by the hour. Pesticide — can't skip it, bollworm and aphids hit every year. I spray three, maybe four times. I handle topping myself in July. Picking I do myself mostly but I'll hire a couple of neighbor women for a few days when the first flush comes in September, maybe 8 hired days total across the season. I'm hoping for 230 kg lint per mu — last year I got 245 but the spring was better.

**Chili (2 mu).** I buy seedlings from the vegetable nursery in town, about 3,000 plants per mu, 400 yuan per mu for the seedlings. Plant early May after the cold snap passes, under plastic mulch. Chili is hungry — I put down 25 kg N per mu split across base and two topdresses, plus potassium because chili needs it or the fruits crack. I drip-irrigate from the well — I put the drip tape in myself three years ago and it saves a lot of water. Five, six irrigations across the season. Pesticide is constant with chili — anthracnose, aphids, whiteflies. Picking starts in July and runs to October. I'll hire help for picking, maybe 15 days of hired labor across those months. I'm targeting 2,000 kg fresh chili per mu — if the market holds at 3 yuan/kg that pays for everything else.

**Mungbean (1.6 mu).** This is the easy one. I plant after the wheat in our village would have come out — late June. Broadcast seed, light disc, maybe 3-4 kg seed per mu. Mungbean doesn't need much — a little DAP at planting, maybe 5 kg N total, and it fixes the rest itself. No irrigation unless it's really dry in July. Harvest in September by hand, thresh with a stick on a tarp. 120 kg per mu is a normal year for me.

**What I'm worried about.** Cash is tight. My son sent 3,000 yuan in March which helps, but inputs for all three crops will run me around 5,000 yuan. The chili is the gamble — if prices drop below 2 yuan/kg like in 2023 I'll lose money on it. Cotton price has been okay but not great. If my back holds up I'll be fine. If I fall sick in picking season, that's the real risk — nobody's picking for me.
